ui.hint.tz:
• The HUD shows local time; the offset is read from the newest save file.
  • If the display differs from the game, correct it above.
  • Counters are not affected.
ui.tz.zones_off: Time zones are disabled in game (g_time_zones 0) → no offset applied
ui.hint.split_on:
• A rest of ≥ 3:00 interrupted by driving is kept as part 1; the next ≥ 9:00 completes the daily rest.
  • A single 11 h block still works as usual.
ui.hint.split_off: Any rest interrupted by driving is discarded regardless of length; the daily rest is always an uninterrupted 11 h.
ui.hint.split_locked: A split rest is in progress (part 1 recorded); switching to single is locked until the day completes or part 1 is cancelled.

ui.hint.auto_break: If you end the break manually it will not re-trigger until the vehicle moves.
ui.hint.offjob:
With no active delivery the app switches to "Off job":
  • Driving is not counted, timers do not advance, buttons are locked.
  • Setting a GPS route starts provisional counting; it becomes permanent when a job is taken, and is reverted if the route is removed without a job.
  • Yard move switches on automatically when a job starts and near the delivery area.
  • Trailer loading/unloading time skips are not counted.
ui.rules_html:
4:30 driving → 0:45 break → 4:30 driving → 11:00 rest (or 3:00 + 9:00).
Everything is measured in game minutes; sleep / ferry / train time skips count as rest. Rest is only reset by driving; yard move and on duty pause it without discarding. Yard move returns to Driving above {kmh} km/h.
ui.hint.skip_html:
Sends g_set_time to the game console.
  • g_console 1 and g_developer 1 must be enabled.
  • It only moves time forward and uses the HUD local time.
  • The button locks when the time zone info is stale or the game is paused.
ui.hint.telemetry_html: Plugin: scs-telemetry.dll → must be in the game's bin\win_x64\plugins folder.
ui.tel.missing: Shared memory not found (game closed or plugin not installed).
ui.hint.window: Position and size are remembered on close.
ui.hint.reset: Resets driving, rest and the day's flow (like a new day).
ui.hint.feedback: Opens a short form; bugs, ideas and requests are collected there.
log.break_part1: Break part 1 recorded ({r}) — another {p2} min before the 4.5 h block ends is enough
log.break_split_done: Split break complete ✓ ({p1} + {p2}) — 4.5 h of driving renewed
ui.split_break: A stop of ≥ 15 min within the 4.5 h block counts as part 1; the next ≥ 30 min break renews the block
ui.hint.split_break:
EU rule: the 45-minute break may be split into at least 15 minutes followed by at least 30 minutes.
  • With part 1 recorded the target becomes 0:30.
  • The part is cleared when the block renews.
ui.part1b.stored: Break part 1 in this block: {p1} → {p2} more minutes are enough
ui.sounds: Play a sound {d} min before driving/rest ends and when it ends
ui.hint.sounds:
One notification sound:
  • Once as early warning.
  • Twice in a row on violation.
  • Once when a break/rest completes.
  • Replace the .wav files in assets/sounds to customise it.
ui.hint.mini:
A small draggable gauge over the game:
  • Status icon, driving / rest time left, next step, three mini bars (block · daily · rest).
  • Game clock, flags, delivery due time and Break / Yard move / Skip buttons.
  • The hotkey swaps it with the main window; its position is remembered.
  • The window is transparent: lower the opacity and the game shows through the strip.
skip.blocked_console: Game console disabled — config.cfg: g_console "1" and g_developer "1"
ui.hint.tour: The first-run tour: explains the screen, the settings tabs and the counting logic step by step.
tour.welcome.b:
One rule: 4:30 driving → 0:45 break → 4:30 driving → 11:00 rest.
  • Everything is counted in game time.
  • With the game running, states are detected from speed automatically.
  • This short tour explains the screen and the logic — the arrow keys work too.
tour.top.b:
• Connection status, your truck and the active job (route · cargo · time to deliver).
  • The clock on the right is the game clock — the same local time as the HUD; the zone is read from the newest save file.
  • Below it your game profile: name · level · company — counters, history and events are kept per profile; switch profiles in the game and the app follows.
  • The gear opens the settings.
  • When a newer version is out, a banner appears under this bar with a download button (can be switched off in Settings → App).
tour.hero.b:
• The label at the top is your state: Driving, On duty, Break or Yard move.
  • The big number is the driving time you have left; while resting it shows rest progress.
  • It turns orange 15 min before the limit and red on a violation.
  • The small icons below are flags: parked, timer stopped, game paused, no delivery…
tour.bars.b:
• Driving block — 4:30 before a break is due.
  • Daily driving — 9:00; the middle mark is 4:30.
  • Rest — target 0:45 break or 11:00 daily; the notch is the 45-minute break threshold.
  • Weekly driving — a fourth bar when the weekly rules are on: 56 h in the week, 90 h over two weeks.
tour.seq.b:
Today's actual flow, box by box:
  • Completed ones ✓, the current one highlighted, the rest planned.
  • With a 3+9 split rest or a 15+30 split break the boxes rearrange accordingly.
tour.btns.b:
• Break: starts rest while the truck is stopped; ends by itself when you move. It also switches on automatically when you stop with little driving time left.
  • Yard move: manoeuvring at loading and delivery areas does not count as driving; it switches on by itself when a job starts and near the destination, off above 40 km/h.
tour.skip.b:
During a break or rest a Skip button appears here.
  • It sends g_set_time to the game console and fast-forwards exactly as much as needed.
  • The console must be enabled in the game (config.cfg: g_console 1, g_developer 1).
  • Otherwise the button stays locked and tells you why.
tour.log.b: Every decision lands here: break started, block renewed, time skip counted as rest, save rollback… If something did not go as expected, look here first.
tour.gear.b: The gear opens a settings panel with four tabs. Let's go through them one by one.
tour.tab_clock.b:
• Clock source: game time or manual (advance the clock yourself when the game is not running).
  • Time zone: the HUD shows the country's local time, OpenTacho reads the zone from the save file; if the display differs from the game you can adjust it by ±1 h.
tour.tab_rules.b:
• Split rest (3+9)
  • Split break (15+30)
  • Automatic break
  • Strict mode: rest counts only with the engine off + parking brake on
  • Violation severity (minor/serious/very serious) and optional virtual fines
  • Weekly rules (optional): 56 / 90 h, 10 h extension, 9 h reduced rest, day spread, weekly rest
  • Off-job mode: with no active delivery the counters stop, rest can still count if you want.
  • Rule set: EU (561/2006) or US (FMCSA HOS: 8 h / 30 min / 11 h / 10 h, 14 h window, 70 h / 8 days) by game, or chosen manually
tour.tab_game.b:
• Recommended game setup: fatigue simulation off, rests skipped from the app.
  • The time frame used by the skip button.
  • Telemetry details: plugin version, game, time scale, save age — look here if the connection or the clock misbehaves.
tour.tab_app.b:
• Language and theme — the Custom theme takes your own background image and colours
  • Sound alerts and voice announcements
  • Mini strip: hotkey, size and background opacity
  • Always on top, resetting the counters, feedback
  • Updates: version, check now, download link
  • Restarting this guide
  • Use on a phone or tablet: LAN sharing, QR code, control from the phone
tour.mini.b:
Ctrl + Num 0 (changeable) swaps the main window for a small draggable gauge over the game.
  • State, time left, mini bars (block · daily · rest · weekly/cycle), clock, flags and the delivery deadline with the planner verdict.
  • Break / Yard move / Skip / Full rest / Weekly rest buttons.
  • Size and background opacity are set in Settings → App.
  • The same key brings the main window back.
tour.done.b: Start the game; with the plugin installed the connection comes up by itself and the counters start working. Safe travels! To see this tour again: Settings → App → Restart the guide.
log.jump_travel: Ferry/train time skip +{d} → counted as rest
fullrest.label: Full rest ({d})
fullrest.sub: advances game time by +{d} · tachograph starts fresh
ui.hist.title: Tachograph history
ui.hist.hint: One row per working day: driving, rest and violations. A day closes when the daily rest completes (or the counters are reset). Job records follow below; the buttons above write days and jobs to files (exports folder next to the exe).
ui.hist.none: No records yet — a day is written here when its daily rest completes.
tour.quick.b:
The four small buttons under the gear:
  • Mini strip — switch to the small in-game overlay without opening settings.
  • Job planner — enter km and delivery time before taking a job to see whether it fits.
  • Tachograph history — driving, rest and violations per day, like a real tachograph printout.
  • Use on a phone or tablet — opens the QR code; a device on the same Wi-Fi follows in its browser.
tour.fullrest.b:
While the truck is stopped a Full rest button appears in the main panel.
  • It sets Off duty and skips the whole 11 h daily rest (9 h as part 2 of a split) in one go.
  • Press it before taking a new job to start with fresh counters.
  • Same rules as Skip: the game console must be enabled.
tour.hist.b:
A day-by-day list like a real tachograph printout; each card is one working day:
  • Start and end time, total driving and rest.
  • Segments (time + duration) and violations (4.5 h block / 9 h daily exceeded, with time and overrun).
  • A day lands here when its daily rest completes or the counters are reset; today's live card stays on top.
  • Jobs: route, driving, breaks, violations, revenue / cancel penalty and lateness for every load.
  • Tachograph printout (PDF + txt) and CSV buttons write everything to the exports folder next to the exe.
tour.setup.b:
The most effective way to use OpenTacho is to take the game's own fatigue mechanic out of the loop.
  1. In the game untick Options → Gameplay → Fatigue simulation — its fatigue clock has nothing to do with the EU rule.
  2. Don't sleep at rest areas / hotels — the game decides how long you sleep, rarely the 11 h a daily rest needs.
  3. When your driving time is up, stop the truck and skip breaks and rests from here with ⏩ Skip or Full rest — the game clock advances by exactly the required amount and the time is credited instantly. This needs the console (config.cfg: g_console 1, g_developer 1).
ui.hint.setup_html:
Most effective use:
  1. In the game keep Options → Gameplay → Fatigue simulation off — the game's fatigue clock doesn't follow the EU rule.
  2. Don't sleep at rest areas / hotels — in-game sleep isn't 11 h.
  3. When your driving time is up, stop the truck and skip breaks and rests with ⏩ Skip / Full rest — the game clock advances by exactly the required amount and the time is credited instantly.
ui.hint.custom:
• Put your own image in the background (JPG, PNG, WebP…); it is downscaled and stored next to the app. Image placement: fill, fit, centre, tile or stretch.
  • Window colour sets the tone of the panels and background, accent colour the headings, buttons and bars; the text colour is chosen automatically.
  • The look is the plain theme's — flat panels, no painted frames; with an image the panels turn slightly translucent so it shows through.
  • Changes apply instantly; the mini strip and the phone page use the same colours.
ui.custom.err_type: Only JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF or BMP images can be used.
ui.weekly_rules: Apply the weekly rules (56 h / 90 h, day spread, weekly rest)
ui.hint.weekly:
Off: only the daily rule runs (4:30 / 0:45 / 11:00). On: the weekly layer of EU 561/2006 is added:
  • Weekly driving 56 h, 90 h in two consecutive weeks (week: Mon 00:00 – Sun 24:00, game time).
  • Extended driving: the daily 9 h may be 10 h twice a week; with the automatic option on, driving past 9 h extends the day by itself while an allowance is left (the limit shows 10:00 up front, the allowance is used once 9 h is exceeded).
  • Reduced rest: the 11 h daily rest may be 9 h three times a week; with the automatic option on, driving off after 9 h of rest counts the day as complete while an allowance is left (the chip in the main panel skips 9 h; waiting for 11 h gives a full rest).
  • Day spread: the daily rest must start no later than 13 h (15 h with a reduced rest) after the day's first driving; shown as "day end" in the main panel.
  • Weekly rest: 45 h (reduced 24 h), starting no later than 6 days after the previous one ended; the button in the main panel skips it in two steps. Compensation is not tracked.
wrest.label: Weekly rest ({d})
wrest.sub: advances game time by +{d} · in two steps

ui.auto_red: Automatic reduced rest: if you drive off after 9 h of rest, the day counts as complete while an allowance is left ({n}/{max} used this week)

ui.plan.title: Job planner
ui.hint.plan: Before taking a job, type the distance and delivery time from the offer: the app simulates breaks and rests with your current allowances and says fits / doesn't fit. With a job accepted (or a GPS route set) leave the fields empty: route time and delivery window are read from the game, and the result also shows in the job line.
plan.src_none: No route — enter km and time
plan.speed_learned: Your average speed: {v} km/h (learned from recent driving)
plan.speed_default: Default average {v} km/h (learned after a few hours of driving)
plan.empty: Enter the distance and delivery time from the offer above.
plan.no_deadline: No delivery time entered: only the total time was computed.
ui.strict_rest: Count breaks and rests only with the engine off and the parking brake on
ui.hint.strict:
Realistic rest condition:
  • When on, minutes spent in Break do not count unless the engine is off and the parking brake is on (they wait like on-duty time).
  • A flag in the main panel shows why nothing is counting.
  • Time skips (sleep, ferry, ⏩ Skip) are not affected.
ui.fines: Show virtual fine amounts in the history (€, approximate)
ui.hint.fines:
Every violation is labelled by the EU classes (in the history panel):
  • Minor: 4.5 h block up to +30 min, daily up to +1 h, weekly up to +4 h.
  • Serious: block up to +1.5 h, daily up to +2 h, weekly up to +14 h.
  • Very serious: beyond that.
  • With virtual fines on an approximate amount is added: minor €150, serious €450, very serious €1200; the week card shows the total and a Pay button.
  • Pay writes a copy of your newest save, with the fine deducted from the bank account, into a new save slot named "OpenTacho: fine paid"; load that save from the game's Load menu and the money is gone. Saving with F5 first is recommended. Real tariffs differ by country — in-game fun only.
ui.voice_fallback: No Windows voice for this language — the default voice is used (add one in Settings → Time & language → Speech)
ui.hint.voice:
Short sentences are spoken in addition to the notification sound:
  • The voice comes from the Windows voices installed on the computer running the app (no internet). A voice matching the app language is picked if installed (e.g. Turkish "Tolga"); otherwise Windows' default voice speaks — add voices in Windows Settings → Time & language → Speech.
  • Spoken: 15 min before driving time ends and when it ends, 15 min before a rest ends, when a break / daily rest / weekly rest completes.
  • Separate volume sliders for the alert sound and the announcements.

flag.strict_brake: strict mode: apply the parking brake
log.strict_rest_on: Strict mode enabled (rest: engine off + parking brake)

voice.daily_done: Daily rest complete. A new day has started.
voice.sample: Fifteen minutes of driving time left.

log.break_done.us: 30-min break complete ✓ — 8 h of driving renewed
log.daily_done.us: 10 h off duty complete ✓ — new day
big.daily_done_sub.us: New day · 8:00 of driving, then a 30-min break
big.daily_sub_rem.us: Driving left now {rem} · then 8:00 of driving
ui.hist.kind.block.us: 8 h of driving without a 30-min break exceeded
ui.weekly_rules.us: Apply the US layer (14 h window, 70 h / 8 days, 34 h restart)
ui.hint.weekly.us:
Off: only the daily rule applies (8:00 / 0:30 / 11:00 / 10:00). On: the other FMCSA limits are added:
  • 14 h window: driving must end 14 hours after the day's first drive; breaks do not extend the window.
  • 70 h / 8 days: on-duty time (driving + waiting / loading) over the last 8 days may not exceed 70 hours.
  • 34 h restart: 34 consecutive hours off duty reset the cycle; a chip appears in the main panel once less than a full day is left.
  • The sleeper-berth split (7/3) and the adverse-conditions extension are not modelled.
log.weekly_on.us: US layer enabled (14 h window, 70 h / 8 days)
ui.window_over: 14 h window over +{r} · 10 h off duty needed
ui.window_idle: The 14 h window starts with the day's first drive
ui.hint.ruleset:
• By game: EU rules in ETS2, US rules in ATS (profile counters are already kept per game).
  • EU 561/2006: 4:30 driving / 0:45 break / 9:00 daily driving / 11:00 rest (+ weekly layer).
  • US FMCSA HOS: 30-min break after 8 h of driving, 11 h driving per day, 10 h off duty (+ 14 h window, 70 h / 8 days, 34 h restart).
ui.us_no_split: The US rule set has no split rest (3+9) or split break (15+30); the sleeper-berth split (7/3) is not modelled.
ui.rules_html.us:
8:00 driving → 0:30 break → 3:00 driving → 10:00 off duty; driving ends 14 h after the day's first drive (with the US layer on).
Everything is measured in game minutes; sleep / ferry / train time skips count as rest. Rest is only reset by driving; yard move and on duty pause it without discarding. Yard move returns to Driving above {kmh} km/h.
tour.welcome.b.us:
One rule: 8:00 driving → 0:30 break → 3:00 driving → 10:00 off duty (US · FMCSA).
  • Everything is counted in game time.
  • With the game running, states are detected from speed automatically.
  • This short tour explains the screen and the logic — the arrow keys work too.
tour.bars.b.us:
• Driving block — 8:00 before a 30-min break is due.
  • Daily driving — 11:00; the middle mark is 8:00.
  • Rest — target 0:30 break or 10:00 off duty; the notch is the 30-minute break threshold.
  • Cycle (8 days) — a fourth bar when the US layer is on: 70 h on duty over 8 days.
ui.hint.update:
• The check reads the latest release info from GitHub (api.github.com); nothing else is sent.
  • Download opens the zip in your browser: extract it over the existing folder; settings and counters are kept.

ui.sec.lan: Use on a phone or tablet
ui.lan.on: Share on the local network — a phone/tablet on the same Wi-Fi follows in its browser
ui.lan.control: Allow control from the phone (Break / Yard move / Skip / Full rest)
ui.lan.scan: Scan the QR code with the phone or type the address into its browser:
ui.lan.off_hint: Sharing is off — switch it on and the QR code appears here.
ui.hint.lan:
• No internet needed; the phone and the PC must be on the same local network (same router/Wi-Fi or the phone's hotspot). On guest networks devices may not see each other.
  • On first use Windows Firewall asks for permission: allow it for private networks.
  • The address carries a random 16-character key; nobody without the key can connect. New code drops old connections. Nothing listens while sharing is off or after the app is closed. Sharing lasts for the session only: it is off after every restart, and every switch-on issues a new code and address.
  • "Add to Home screen" on the phone opens it like an app; the page keeps the screen awake, plays a sound and vibrates on alerts, and has history and planner tabs.
mob.readonly: Control from the phone is off (enable it in the app)
mob.forbidden: Invalid or outdated link — create a new QR code in the app and scan it again.
